items.evidence: After the reload, the spec asserts the rule count is 0 and the empty-rules message shows (diff lines 106-111). Both would fail if the rule delete never reached the server.
Criterion 1 is asserted at lines 99-102. Criterion 2 is asserted at lines 106-111: after the reload there are no rules and the name is still PROMOTIONS.catalogue.name.
No existing page object covers promotions. findPromotionId is new, uses gql/adminToken from e2e/lib/graphql.ts, and follows the findOrderId pattern.
No fixed waits. The only waits are nameInput.waitFor() and waiting for the dialog to be hidden.
Imports test/expect from fixtures/test.ts and is not tagged parallel(). It writes nothing to the cache or dumps.
Every locator is a data-test-id that exists in src. The dialog's button is scoped to deleteRuleDialog, and the rule's delete button is scoped to rules.
Uses the promotion the orders scenario already provides. The only GraphQL call is a read lookup by name.
The promotion id is looked up at test time by the scenario's known name. No populatedb values are used.
Uses the fixture's default admin session. There is no UI login and no credentials in the spec.
typecheck.txt reports exit 0, and the spec lives in e2e/tests/discounts/.
All locators and the multi-step delete action live on PromotionPage. The spec only calls page reload.
Members are readonly fields initialised from this.page, and the class uses constructor(readonly page: Page) {}.
Has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments (lines 89, 96).
One test for the story, with a test.step for each stage.
The title describes the behaviour and carries #e2e.
A header comment (lines 78-81) says what the spec covers and why.
Every assertion is web-first (toHaveValue, toHaveCount, toContainText).
Uses ORDERS_SCENARIO and PROMOTIONS.catalogue.name. The empty-state text is UI copy, not a scenario value.
No cleanup steps and no unique names.
No custom timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep .ts, and only the Page type comes from @playwright/test.
The gql call is typed and there are no any or casts.
The comments explain reasons, such as why there is only one rule and that the dialog closes once the server has deleted it. None narrate the code.

structured_output.summary: Submission 4e7e3762 meets all 23 checklist items (B1–B10 and M1–M13). The spec opens the E2E Tee sale promotion using an id looked up by name, through a new findPromotionId helper typed against PROMOTIONS. It deletes the rule using test ids that exist in the dashboard source, with locators scoped to the rule and the dialog. It then checks that no rules remain, both right after confirming and after a reload; the post-reload check also confirms the promotion keeps its name. That reload check covers both acceptance criteria and would fail if the deletion never reached the server. The new PromotionPage follows the suite's page-object style, the type check passed with no errors, and the spec reads like the existing order specs.
